hostLink.fixIntro: Run these on {{host}} itself, not in this terminal, or hand the prompt to Claude Code or Codex on that machine.
hostLink.install: If it is stopped, reinstall and start it:
hostLink.prompt:
The Oppenheimer runner on {{host}} has lost its link to Oppenheimer. Help me get it back.

- First tell me which machine you are on (uname -n, whoami). If it is not {{host}}, stop.
- Run ~/.local/bin/oppenheimer-runner status and show me what it prints.
- Read the last 50 lines of ~/.oppenheimer/log/runner.log and ~/.oppenheimer/log/runner.err.log
  and tell me what went wrong.
- Do not reinstall, uninstall or run anything as root unless I say so. If the service is
  stopped, propose ~/.local/bin/oppenheimer-runner install and wait for my go-ahead.

share.title: Share “{{name}}”
share.description: A link that opens this session’s terminal for someone outside your workspace. It works for as long as you can open the session, until it expires or you revoke it.
share.readHint: See the terminal live. Nothing they type reaches it.
share.writeHint: Type into the terminal: a shell on your host, as you.
share.peopleHint: They sign in with one of these verified emails.
share.accountsHint: Anyone with the link and an Oppenheimer account.
share.anyoneHint: No sign-in needed. Whoever has the link has the terminal.
share.emailsHint: Separate them with commas, spaces or new lines.
share.peopleInvalid: Enter at least one email, and only emails.
share.writeWarning: Anyone who opens this link can run commands on your host as you. Prefer naming the people, and a short expiry.
share.writeNote: The people you name can run commands on your host as you.
share.failed: The link could not be created.
share.onceOnly: Copy it now: it is shown only once. If it is lost, revoke it and make another.
share.listFailed: The links could not be loaded.
share.revokeFailed: The link could not be revoked.
